resolutions: Pronominal NNCs remain absolutive NNCs; they do not acquire the ordinary NNC possessive-State choices.
The entered pronominal source identifies the lexical family, while person and context automatically select the required eh or yeh realization.
A stem-internal plural n belongs to the predicate stem and remains separate from the subject-number connector outside the stem.
Sounded and silent number forms are genuine licensed choices; they do not change the identity of the pronominal source.
The doubled first-plural construction is restricted to first-plural compound personal NNCs and cannot spread to other subjects.
Interrogative force belongs to the typed clause context: an inherently interrogative form loses that force outside initial position.
A separate dependent in and a fused elliptical in are different constructions and remain separate user choices.
Demonstrative singular and plural may share a written surface while retaining different typed subject-number structures.
Human use of itlah requires its explicit licensed context; animate selection or a documentary example cannot silently authorize it.
A quantitive source keeps its entered lexical identity while the application automatically selects a conditioned matrix allomorph for the chosen plural formation.
Normal internal-n quantity plurals and lexically licensed plain variants remain different choices; an unwitnessed plain variant stays blocked.
Second-plural subject assimilation is an automatic boundary result and is not a separate user choice or a change to the quantitive stem.
Sentence particles and adverbial modifiers combine outside the completed NNC nucleus; they change the sentence Result without rewriting the NNC formula.
The shortened mo-ch quantity stem may form a simple plural or serve as the embed of mo-ch-eh-huā without collapsing those two source structures.
